content: As competitors in the South African market align with these global technological trajectories, the deployment of sophisticated VoIP and UCaaS solutions is anticipated to serve as a primary vehicle for enterprise digital transformation and operational efficiency. The successful deployment and optimal performance of UCaaS and VoIP solutions are intrinsically linked to robust network management strategies. Ultimately, the core services offered by telecommunications competitors in South Africa are undergoing a profound transformation driven by the necessity for integrated, intelligent, and highly reliable communication ecosystems. Mining companies may hesitate to deploy capital-intensive digital transformation initiatives, including advanced telecommunications networks, Internet of Things (IoT) deployments, and automated managed services, until their long-term operational rights are securely registered under the new system. As operations evolve to meet modern demands, robust connectivity has emerged as a cornerstone for enabling these technological transformations. Reliable and resilient communication systems are no longer viewed as optional upgrades but are recognized as essential prerequisites for maximizing operational efficiency, safety, and sustainability across both surface and underground mining environments [7] [34] . The development and implementation of these systems between 2020 and 2024 were characterized by steady advancements, heavily influenced by growing digitalization trends and the necessity to support increasingly complex operational frameworks. The evolution of mining communication infrastructure in South Africa has been heavily influenced by strategic alliances, public-private partnerships, and long-term capital commitments aimed at accelerating digital transformation. Historical analyses have long discussed digital transformation and sustainability as foundational concepts shaping communication infrastructure in mining, though detailed analyses of the South African market closer to 2026 remain scarce [54] . Empirical data from the period between 2020 and 2024 corroborates this rapid modernization. Furthermore, by participating in public-private dialogues and aligning with the overarching goals of the 2035 broadband expansion plan, Vcom can position itself as a central pillar of South Africa’s digital transformation.
